LESSON: ADDITION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.2: Addition
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Addition, part of Numbers in Grade 5 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How can you estimate the sum of given numbers? 2. 2. How can you create patterns in addition?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. multiply up to a 3-digit number by up to a 2-digit number in real-life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Addition in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. estimate product by rounding off numbers to the nearest ten in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Addition in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. make patterns involving multiplication of numbers with product not exceeding 1000 in in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Addition in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate use of multiplication in real life.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Addition in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. multiply up to a 3-digit number by up to a 2-digit number in real-life situations,

   Addition helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. estimate product by rounding off numbers to the nearest ten in different situations,

   Addition helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. make patterns involving multiplication of numbers with product not exceeding 1000 in in different situations,

   Addition helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate use of multiplication in real life.

   Addition helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work out the sum of three 6-digit numbers without regrouping up to 1,000,000 using place charts or any other resource, collaborates with others to work out the sum of two 6-digit numbers with double regrouping with the number not more than 1,000,000 using place value apparatus or any other resource, estimate sums by rounding off the addends to the nearest hundred and thousand, come up with patterns involving addition of numbers up to a sum of 1,000,000, play games involving addition of numbers using digital devices and other resources. 1. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work out the sum of three 6-digit numbers without regrouping up to 1,000,000 using place charts or any other resource, collaborates with others to work out the sum of two 6-digit numbers with double regrouping with the number not more than 1,000,000 using place value apparatus or any other resource, estimate sums by rounding off the addends to the nearest hundred and thousand, come up with patterns involving addition of numbers up to a sum of 1,000,000, play games involving addition of numbers using digital devices and other resources. 1. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Addition together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Unity: learner collaborates with others to work out the sum of two 6-digit numbers.

• Responsibility: learner takes roles individually to achieve common solutions in addition of numbers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Social cohesion: leaner works with peers in using digital resources for learning the addition of numbers.

Link to other learning areas

The learner is able to relate the concept of addition to value addition in Agriculture and Nutrition.

Main points to remember:

1. multiply up to a 3-digit number by up to a 2-digit number in real-life situations,
2. estimate product by rounding off numbers to the nearest ten in different situations,
3. make patterns involving multiplication of numbers with product not exceeding 1000 in in different situations,
4. appreciate use of multiplication in real life.
